title: Grounds & Powered Equipment Safety
blurb: Using mowers, strimmers and chainsaws safely: training, PPE, clearing the area, refuelling and never defeating a guard.
siteNotes: Which grounds machines each person is trained and authorised to use
Where PPE, including eye protection and ear defenders, is kept
Who to report faulty machines to, and how they are taken out of use
Where fuel is stored and where refuelling is done
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-58. Training and competence: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER), reg. 9; guards and safe condition under PUWER; PPE under the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992.

cards.title: Grounds & Powered Equipment Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- use only machines you are trained and authorised to operate
- wear the right PPE and clear the area first
- refuel safely and report faults or missing guards

cards.title: Powerful tools need respect
cards.body:
Keeping our grounds looking beautiful means using powerful equipment: mowers, strimmers, hedge trimmers, leaf blowers and chainsaws. These tools save huge amounts of time, but they can cause serious injuries in a moment's carelessness.

They demand respect, training and the right protective kit.

cards.title: Trained and authorised only
cards.body:
Only use equipment you have been trained and authorised to operate. Some tools, chainsaws especially, need proper certificated training. They are not something to "have a go" with.

> If you are not trained on a machine, do not use it, and never let an untrained person pick one up.

cards.title: Wear it every time
cards.body: Wear the correct PPE every time. Chainsaw work needs specialist protective trousers.

cards.title: Check the machine, clear the area
cards.body:
Before you start, check the machine and its guards are in good order. Clear the area of people, pets and debris.

> Thrown stones and cuttings injure bystanders as well as operators.

cards.title: Refuel safely, keep guards on
cards.body:
Refuel safely, with the engine switched off and cooled. Keep guards in place at all times, and never remove or defeat a safety guard.

If a machine is faulty, damaged or a guard is missing, take it out of use and report it.

left.title: Do
items: Refuel with the engine off and cooled
Take faulty machines out of use

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Only use machines you are trained and authorised to use
- Chainsaws need certificated training
- Wear the right PPE and clear people, pets and debris first
- Refuel with the engine off and cooled
- Never defeat a guard. Faulty means out of use and reported

cards.q: You should only use powered equipment you have been:
options: Curious about, and watched someone use
cards.why: Only use equipment you have been trained and authorised to operate.
Chainsaws especially need proper certificated training. They are not something to have a go with.

cards.q: Which two items of PPE should you wear for powered grounds equipment?
cards.why: Typical PPE includes eye protection, ear defenders, gloves, protective boots and close-fitting clothing.

cards.q: You should clear the area of people, pets and debris before starting.
cards.why: Thrown stones and cuttings injure bystanders as well as operators.

cards.q: When should you refuel a machine?
options: While it is running, to save time
With the engine off and cooled
While it is still hot, so it is ready
Once it has been started again
cards.why: Refuel with the engine switched off and cooled.

cards.q: It is fine to remove a safety guard to make a job quicker.
cards.why: Never remove or defeat a safety guard. Keep guards in place at all times.

cards.q: Why should bystanders be kept clear of powered equipment?
options: Thrown stones and cuttings can injure them
They could slow the job down
cards.why: Thrown stones and cuttings injure bystanders as well as operators.

cards.q: A machine has a missing guard. It should be:
options: Taken out of use and reported
Left for someone else to find
cards.why: A faulty or damaged machine, or one with a missing guard, is taken out of use and reported.

cards.q: If you are not trained on a machine, you should not use it.
cards.why: If you are not trained on a machine, do not use it, and never let an untrained person pick one up.

cards.q: Guards should be kept in place at all times.
cards.why: Keep guards in place at all times and never defeat a safety guard.
